saturnine

SAT-ur-nyne · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Saturnine is slow and gloomy in one's settled temperament or habitual manner.

The professor's saturnine manner made even good news sound like bad news.

Example

Behind his saturnine exterior, the old sea captain rarely smiled, even when his crew returned home safely.

The captain's habitual gloominess wasn't caused by any one event -- it's simply his whole manner, which is exactly what saturnine describes.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

gloomy: Gloomy describes a dark, low, dispirited mood -- the way anyone might feel on a bad day. Saturnine goes much further: not one dark afternoon but a settled temperament, a gloominess so habitual that it colors everything a person does, year in and year out.

dour: Dour describes a stern, grim, unsmiling manner -- a dour judge seems harsh and forbidding to everyone in the room. Saturnine is quieter and sadder: a settled dark mood rather than outward sternness, and a saturnine person can still be perfectly gentle company.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

buoyant: cheerful and lighthearted

Where it sits · how dark and settled the mood is — serious → saturnine → brooding

serious vs. saturnine: Being serious just means not joking around; being saturnine describes a lasting, gloomy temperament that colors everything a person does.

brooding vs. saturnine: A saturnine person is simply gloomy by nature; a brooding one is actively dwelling on dark or troubling thoughts.

Build the Word

The pieces

Put it together

Put it together: Saturnine isn't built from a root and suffix -- it comes straight from the planet Saturn. In old astrology, anyone born under Saturn's influence was believed to grow up cold, slow, and gloomy.

Use the root in a new word: Saturday

Use the root in a new word: Saturday: The same planet also gives us the ordinary word Saturday -- so saturnine and Saturday share a namesake, not a grammatical root.

Strength Check

Word Choice

Saturnine describes a lasting personality trait -- a naturally gloomy manner -- distinct from this unit's "petulance" (a childish, temporary bad mood) and "blase" (jaded unconcern, not gloom).
